extracted.intended_audience: recipients and subrecipients of Federal awards; grants administrators, financial and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on which costs are allowable or unallowable under Uniform Guidance (2 C.F.R. §200 Subpart E), including required conditions, documentation, and allocation rules for recipients/subrecipients of Federal awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.440 Exchange rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost increases for fluctuations in exchange rates are allowable costs subject to the availability of funding; prior approval required only when change results in need for additional Federal funding or significant reduction in project scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal agency must ensure adequate funds are available before approving to avoid Antideficiency Act violations. Recipients/subrecipients must review local currency gains to determine need for additional Federal funding before award expiration. Subsequent adjustments for currency increases are allowable only when recipient/subrecipient provides adequate source documentation from a commonly used source in effect at the time the expense was made, and sufficient Federal funds are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.441 Fines, penalties, damages and other settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs resulting from recipient or subrecipient violations of, alleged violations of, or failure to comply with laws and regulations are unallowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: such costs may be allowable when incurred as a result of compliance with specific provisions of the Federal award, or with the prior written approval of the Federal agency. See §200.435 for related legal cost limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.442 Fundraising and investment management costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of organized fundraising and investment-management activities are generally unallowable, with limited exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (a) Organized fundraising (campaigns, endowment drives, solicitation of gifts) unallowable; fundraising costs for meeting Federal program objectives allowable with prior written approval. (b) Investment counsel/staff costs to enhance investment income unallowable except when associated with investments covering pension, self-insurance, or other funds that include Federal participation. (c) Costs related to physical custody/control of monies and securities are allowable. (d) Both allowable and unallowable fundraising/investment activities must be allocated appropriate share of indirect costs per §200.413.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.443 Gains and losses on the disposition of depreciable assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Gains and losses on sale, retirement, or other disposition of depreciable property must be included in the year they occur as credits or charges to the asset cost grouping(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amount equals difference between amount realized and undepreciated basis. Gains/losses must not be recognized as a separate credit/charge when (1) processed through depreciation account and reflected in depreciation allowable under §§200.436 and 200.439; (2) property exchanged as part of purchase price of similar item and taken into account in new item's depreciation basis; (3) loss results from failing to maintain proper insurance (except §200.447); (4) compensation provided through use allowances instead of depreciation; (5) extraordinary or bulk sales considered case-by-case. Gains/losses from disposition of other property must be excluded in computing Federal award costs. Proceeds from disposal of assets acquired with Federal funds distributed per §§200.310–200.316.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.444 General costs of government
rubrics_metrics.description: For states, local governments, and Indian Tribes, general costs of government are unallowable except as provided in §200.475.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unallowable examples include: (1) salaries/expenses of governor/chief executive; (2) salaries/expenses of state legislature, tribal council, local governmental bodies; (3) judicial branch costs; (4) prosecutorial activities unless treated as direct cost to specific program if authorized by statute/regulation (other legal activities may be allowable per §200.435); (5) other general services normally provided to public (fire, police) unless provided as direct cost under program statute. Indian Tribes and COGs may include up to 50% of salaries/expenses directly attributable to managing/operating Federal programs by chief executive and staff in the indirect cost calculation without documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.445 Goods or services for personal use
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of goods or services for the personal use of recipient's or subrecipient's employees are unallowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is true regardless of whether the cost is reported as taxable income. Housing costs (depreciation, maintenance, utilities, furnishings, rent), housing allowances, and personal living expenses are allowable only as direct costs and must be approved in advance by the Federal agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.446 Idle facilities and idle capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of idle facilities or idle capacity are generally unallowable except under specified circumstances; definitions provided for facilities, idle facilities, and idle capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions clarify measurement of idle capacity. (b) Idle facilities costs unallowable except to extent necessary to meet fluctuating workload and allocated appropriately, or when facilities were necessary when acquired and now idle due to unforeseeable changes—allowable for a reasonable period, ordinarily not exceeding one year depending on initiative to use/lease/dispose. (c) Idle capacity costs are normal business costs and allowable provided capacity reasonably anticipated necessary to carry out Federal award purpose or was originally reasonable and not subject to reduction by use on other awards, subletting, renting, or sale; widespread idle capacity may be considered idle facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.447 Insurance and indemnification
rubrics_metrics.description: Insurance costs required/approved by the Federal award are allowable; other insurance costs are allowable only subject to limitations and conditions; indemnification limited to what is expressly provided in the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key limitations: (b)(1) types/extent/cost must follow recipient's written policy and sound business practices; (b)(2) costs covering risk of loss of Government property unallowable except with agency approval; (b)(3) business-interruption insurance must exclude management fees; (b)(4) life insurance on trustees/officers allowable only if additional compensation; (b)(5) insurance to correct defects unallowable; (b)(6) medical malpractice insurance allowable only when program involves human subjects or training, treated as direct cost. (c) Actual losses that could have been covered by permissible insurance unallowable unless expressly authorized; minor losses not covered by insurance (spoilage, breakage) allowable. (d) Contributions to self-insurance reserves allowable subject to actuarial/prudential requirements (present value limits, earnings credited to reserves, biennial reserve analyses, documentation/justification for excess reserves, equitable allocations, refunds to Federal Government when transferred). (e) Insurance refunds must be credited against insurance costs in year received. (f) Indemnification clauses: Federal Government indemnifies recipient only as expressly provided, except for (c) minor loss allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.448 Intellectual property
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of patent and copyright costs, and royalties, determining allowability depending on relation to Federal award requirements and government rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent/copyright securing costs allowable when preparing disclosures/reports required by award and searching art to extent necessary; costs of preparing documents and prosecution of US patent application allowable where Government requires title or royalty-free license; general counseling services allowable. Unallowable: preparing disclosures/reports/searches not required by award; filing/prosecuting foreign patents or US patents where award does not require conveying title/license. Royalties necessary for proper performance allowable unless Government already has license/right to free use, patent adjudicated invalid/unenforceable, or expired. Exercise care on royalties obtained through less-than-arm's-length bargaining (payments to affiliates, agreements entered in contemplation of award, agreements after award). For patents/copyrights formerly owned by recipient, royalty allowed must not exceed cost that would have been allowed had recipient retained ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.449 Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: General rule: interest on borrowed capital, temporary use of endowment funds, or use of recipient's own funds is unallowable, except financing costs to acquire/construct/replace capital assets are allowable subject to detailed requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capital assets defined in §200.1; intangible assets include patents and computer software for fiscal years beginning on/after Jan 1, 2016. For software projects, only interest attributable to portion capitalized per GAAP is allowable. Requirements for allowability include: (1) capital assets used in support of Federal awards; (2) allowable asset costs limited to fair market value from unrelated third party; (3) financing via arm's-length transaction or reimburse actual interest at such rate; (4) limit claims to least expensive alternative (e.g., lease-equivalent); (5) expense/capitalize per GAAP; (6) offset earnings from invested borrowed funds against allowable interest; (7) for debt > $1M (unless initial equity ≥25%), reduce claims by imputed interest on excess cash flow and impute interest monthly per specified Treasury bill rate method; (8) interest on fully depreciated asset unallowable. Additional timing/eligibility restrictions for states/local governments/Indian Tribes, IHEs, and nonprofit organizations (dates specified). Nonprofits under full CAS coverage follow CAS 414 and CAS 417 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.450 Lobbying
rubrics_metrics.description: Lobbying/influencing activities associated with obtaining Federal awards and certain lobbying costs are unallowable, subject to statutory and regulatory restrictions and specific exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (a) Costs of certain influencing activities associated with obtaining grants/cooperative agreements/contracts/loans unallowable; governed by 31 U.S.C. 1352 and OMB guidance. (b) Executive lobbying costs to improperly influence Federal executive employees regarding an award or regulatory matter are unallowable. (c) For nonprofits and IHEs, unallowable activities include influencing elections, supporting political organizations, attempting to influence introduction/enactment/modification of pending legislation, influencing executive decisions on signing/vetoing legislation, and legislative liaison activities when in support of or in preparation for unallowable lobbying. (2) Exceptions: technical/factual presentations in response to documented request; lobbying to influence state legislation to directly reduce cost or avoid material impairment; activities specifically authorized by statute; activities excepted by IRS provisions (nonpartisan analysis, broad examinations, legislator-requested technical information). (3) When seeking indirect cost reimbursement, total lobbying costs must be identified separately in the indirect cost rate proposal and thereafter treated as unallowable per §200.413. (4) Certification of compliance required as part of annual indirect cost rate proposal. (5) Recordkeeping exception: no time logs/calendars required when employee's lobbying ≤25% of compensated hours in a calendar month and recipient hasn't materially misstated costs in prior five years; when conditions met, absence of additional records won't be basis for disallowance. Federal agency, in consultation with OMB, must establish procedures for resolving interpretive questions in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.451 Losses on other awards or contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Any excess costs over income under any other award or contract are unallowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes recipient/subrecipient contributed portion by cost-sharing agreements, under-recoveries through flat indirect cost negotiations, and excess of costs over authorized funding levels transferred from one award to another. All such losses are not allowable indirect costs and must be included in appropriate indirect cost rate base for allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.452 Maintenance and repair costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs for utilities, insurance, security, necessary maintenance, janitorial services, repair, or upkeep of buildings and equipment are allowable provided they neither add permanent value nor appreciably prolong intended life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs that add permanent value or appreciably prolong life are capital expenditures and must be treated per §200.439. These maintenance/repair costs are allowable only to the extent not paid through rental or other agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.453 Materials and supplies costs, including costs of computing devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs for materials, supplies, and fabricated parts necessary for performance of a Federal award are allowable, with specified charging and valuation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purchased materials/supplies charged at actual prices net of credits; withdrawals from stores charged at actual net cost under recognized, consistently applied pricing methods; incoming transportation charges allowable. Materials/supplies used for performance may be charged as direct costs. Charging computing devices as direct costs is allowable for devices essential and allocable, but not solely dedicated, to performance of the Federal award. Federally-donated/furnished materials used in performing the award must be used without charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.454 Memberships, subscriptions, and professional activity costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Memberships in business, technical, and professional organizations and subscriptions to business/professional/technical periodicals are allowable; some memberships are unallowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memberships in civic/community organizations are allowable. Memberships in country clubs, social/dining clubs are unallowable. Memberships in organizations whose primary purpose is lobbying are unallowable (see §200.450).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.455 Organization costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of establishing or reorganizing an organization (incorporation fees, brokers' fees, promoters' fees, professional fees) are unallowable except with prior Federal agency approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs to persuade employees regarding union organizing are unallowable. Data and evaluation costs (gathering, storing, managing, analyzing, securing, sharing, publishing data; building integrated data systems; evaluations; evidence reviews; evaluation planning; conducting evaluations; sharing results) are allowable and listed as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.456 Participant support costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant support costs are allowable when correctly classified and documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification of items as participant support costs must be documented in recipient's/subrecipient's written policies and procedures and treated consistently across all Federal awards. See §200.1 for definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.457 Plant and security costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary and reasonable expenses for protection and security of facilities, personnel, and work products are allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowable items include wages and uniforms of security personnel; equipment; barriers; protective (non-military) gear/devices/equipment; contractual security services; and consultants. Capital expenditures for plant security are subject to §200.439.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.458 Pre-award costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-award costs incurred before the start date of the Federal award may be allowable only under strict conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-award costs must be incurred directly pursuant to negotiation and in anticipation of the Federal award and necessary for efficient/timely performance of scope of work. Allowable only to extent they would have been allowed if incurred after start date and only with written approval of Federal agency. If approved, charged to initial budget period of the award unless agency specifies otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.459 Professional service costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of professional and consultant services by qualified non-employees are allowable when reasonable and not contingent on recovery from the Federal Government, subject to multiple factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors to consider (no single factor determinative): (1) nature/scope of service relative to requirement; (2) necessity of contracting considering recipient capability; (3) past pattern of such costs pre-award; (4) impact of Federal awards on recipient's business; (5) proportion of Federal work to total business; (6) whether service can be more economically performed by direct employment; (7) qualifications and customary fees; (8) adequacy of contractual agreement (description, time estimate, rate, termination). Retainer fees must be supported by evidence of bona fide services available or rendered in addition to these factors. Legal and related services limited under §200.435.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.460 Proposal costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal costs (preparing bids, proposals, applications for potential awards) are generally treated as indirect costs allocated to all current activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes developing data necessary to support bids/proposals. Proposal costs of the current accounting period (successful and unsuccessful) normally treated as indirect costs and allocated to all current activities. No proposal costs of past accounting periods may be allocated to the current period.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 200.461 Publication and printing costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication and printing costs, including distribution and promotion, are allowable, with specific treatment for page charges and article processing charges (APCs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (a) Publication costs for electronic and print media including distribution, promotion, general handling are allowable and should be allocated as indirect costs if not identifiable with a particular cost objective. (b) Page charges, APCs, open access fees for professional journal and peer-reviewed publications resulting from a Federal award are allowable where (1) publications report work supported by the Federal Government, and (2) charges are levied impartially on all items published by the journal. Recipient may charge the Federal award during closeout for publication/sharing costs if costs were not incurred during the period of performance.
